service.clear.explain: Clears this service's cache and site data: HTTP cache, localStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage and service workers. Cookies and other services are left alone. A service that keeps its sign-in in localStorage will sign you out of it. Its service worker is removed, so web push notifications that depend on it need subscribing again. Scripts and styles this tab has already loaded may still be used; if the service still looks out of date afterwards, reload the console page.

help.title: Connection help · for you and your agent
help.intro: Use the form for a web page, a built-in plugin for a supported service, or a plugin folder for a custom integration.
help.pages.title: Connect a web page
help.pages.step1: Start the service and check that its address opens in your browser. For example, http://127.0.0.1:3000/. hostdeck does not start the service for you.
help.pages.step2: In the form below, choose Embed for a web page on this machine or the local network. Choose Link to open any HTTP or HTTPS address in a new tab.
help.pages.step3: Enter its address and an optional name, then choose Add. It appears immediately; open it from the sidebar. Dragging an address onto the console also adds an embedded page.
help.plugins.title: Connect a plugin
help.plugins.step1: For a built-in plugin below, read its setup instructions, start its service if needed, then choose Add and confirm. It takes effect immediately.
help.plugins.step2: For a custom plugin, create a uniquely named folder (for example, my-service) inside the actual plugin directory below, and save plugin.yaml in it. This example reads the status field of a JSON response; replace the address and field with your service’s values.
help.plugins.step3: After manual file changes, run hostdeck plugin reload --url CONSOLE_ORIGIN. Restart hostdeck with the same data directory and address if needed. Refreshing the browser alone does not reload files. Check Pages & plugins for loading errors, then check the card or page.
help.plugins.trust: Only use plugin programs you trust: they run with your permissions. Custom plugins can provide JSON cards and details or connect existing web pages; they do not serve their own HTML. schema: 1 is implemented, but the format may change before the first release.
help.agent.title: Let an agent connect it
help.agent.intro: Copy a prompt into an agent that can run commands on this computer. Then tell it the service name, address and what you want to show. Copying only copies text; it does not change your data.
help.agent.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into your agent and describe the service to connect.
help.agent.copyFailed: Could not access the clipboard. The prompt is selected below; copy it manually.
help.agent.pages: Connect an existing web page. First check that its address opens. page add --url ORIGIN --address URL --name NAME --mode proxy embeds an HTTP/HTTPS page on this machine or the local network; --mode link opens any HTTP/HTTPS page in a new tab. hostdeck does not start the service. Before adding, use plugin list --url ORIGIN to inspect data.installed (proxy/link URLs and names) and avoid duplicates; page add derives the folder ID from the host and port (adding -2, -3 on collision) and returns the assigned ID in data.id. To edit an existing page, use page update --url ORIGIN --id ID with only the requested --name, --icon, --proxy OR --link (not --mode or --address), and --card-url only for an existing HTTP card. Back up its plugin.yaml outside the active plugin directory first, then remove the temporary backup once the update succeeds; the API preserves comments, commands and unrelated fields. CLI changes reload immediately and report the actual installed ID, path and state. A loaded plugin does not prove the external service is healthy.
help.agent.plugins: For a read-only list of running processes, use the built-in processes plugin; it includes programs without listening ports, shows executable path, parent name, UTC start time, uptime, threads and accumulated CPU time alongside CPU/memory, and offers no process actions. Prefer a suitable built-in plugin: plugin catalog --url ORIGIN lists available IDs and setup instructions, and plugin install --url ORIGIN --id ID installs one. For a custom plugin, create its source folder outside the active plugin directory, save plugin.yaml and any scripts there, then use plugin validate --from SOURCE and plugin install --url ORIGIN --id UNIQUE_ID --from SOURCE. Validation uses the CLI process environment and never runs scripts. Installation validates and copies into the actual directory discovered from the selected console, refuses existing enabled or disabled IDs, symlinks and recursive sources, then reloads immediately. Only local folders are supported; nothing is downloaded. The following example creates and removes a temporary source for a new my-service plugin expecting a JSON status field. Replace its URL, field and name. For existing plugins, back up the folder outside the active plugin directory, edit only requested fields/scripts, validate that folder and run plugin reload --url ORIGIN. Keep comments, commands and unrelated settings. plugin enable/disable --url ORIGIN --id ID changes hostdeck loading, not the external service.
help.agent.contract: Current manifest contract (schema: 1; may change before the first release): name is required; provide at least one of page, card or detail. page has proxy OR link; page and detail cannot coexist, but either can have a card. card.http makes a GET request; value and optional rows use gjson paths; label is display text; interval defaults to 1m; warn/error each select one of above, below, equals or not. card.exec.command, detail.exec.command and actions.exec.command are argv arrays; a sibling exec.windows array replaces command on Windows. Commands run in the plugin folder with hostdeck's environment and have 30 seconds. stdout holds exactly one JSON value and nothing after it; diagnostics go to stderr. An unknown field is an error, and an exit code other than 0 shows only the last line of stderr, so report a failure as {"error":"Reason"} with exit code 0. Card JSON: {"status":"ok","value":42,"label":"Count","rows":[{"name":"Queue","value":3,"status":"warn"}]} or {"error":"Reason"}. A row value may be a string, a number or localized text such as {"en":"up","zh-CN":"已运行"}; a string or number still reaches the page as a string. detail.exec prints {"items":[{"id":"item-1","name":"Item","status":"ok","value":"ready","fields":[{"name":"Path","value":"/example"}],"log":"text","actions":[{"id":"open","label":"Open"}]}]} (id is required and unique; name is required and must contain nonblank text; status, value, label, fields, log, logAvailable and actions are optional; items[].label is shown beside the value and left out of the compact list; logAvailable true means a log can be loaded for that item: opening it runs the detail program again with HOSTDECK_DETAIL_ITEM set to the item id and prints that one item with its log, or {"error":"Reason"} when the id is unknown; when HOSTDECK_DETAIL_ITEM is unset the read is the list, log may be omitted, and the read before an action is this list read; the id is data, not a path; a newline or an id longer than 256 bytes is refused before the program runs). actions requires detail; actions.exec receives <action-id> <item-id> and may print {"message":"Done"} or {"error":"Reason"}. Human text can be a string or an object keyed by en and zh-CN. Windows PowerShell scripts use UTF-8 with BOM and output UTF-8. Only run trusted programs; plugins have the user’s permissions. Secrets in HTTP URLs/headers must be ${env:NAME}, supplied to the hostdeck process; never put tokens in files or output. Do not change layout.json, ports.json or other plugins as part of this connection. Optional detail fields: presentation is compact; note is localized text shown only when items is empty and groups are present; groups is an ordered array of {id,label}; items[].group refers to a declared group. Group IDs are unique and nonblank, all is reserved; every item needs a group when groups are present. Existing plugins can omit these fields; using them requires a newer hostdeck. Detail item value and fields[].value accept strings, numbers, or localized en/zh-CN text objects; omit optional new fields for older hostdeck versions. The native Docker plugin uses ["@hostdeck","docker","card"] or detail and needs Docker CLI plus a running local engine. It is independent of jobs, refuses remote endpoints and does not start Docker on installation. Docker actions use ["@hostdeck","docker","action"]; only start for created/exited containers and restart for running ones. Treat item IDs as opaque: they bind the local connection and full container ID. Timeouts may leave an engine action continuing; refresh to confirm. The scheduled-tasks plugin uses separate tasks.json (version: 1 and a tasks array), documented in docs/TASKS.md. Confirmed manual run/stop, results and bounded logs are available; cron/interval scheduling and Pause/Resume are available while hostdeck runs, without catch-up or automatic retries. Installation creates an empty task list; task fields do not belong in plugin.yaml. Scheduled-task records and logs stay in that plugin's data/. Never overwrite corrupt state. Interrupted tasks stay paused; Resume only probes whether the old process tree is clear and never kills old PIDs. If cleanup is uncertain, inspect locally and explicitly reload. Service observations are a console capability for matching built-in jobs/listeners/manual execution configurations, not new manifest or output fields. A familiar folder ID grants no file-reading permission. data/service-observations/ belongs to the actual console directory, outside plugins; do not edit its records, remove active capture data, or overwrite installed plugins to enable this feature. Manual restart prepares capacity and a private detached collector before stop; collection survives console exit. Existing third-party log/logAvailable remain one-shot. Update the executable and refresh the console; only explicitly update jobs helpers when the owner requests it.
help.agent.finish: Use plugin list --url ORIGIN to inspect data.installed (loaded, broken and error). Native CLI mutations reload immediately. After manual file changes use plugin reload --url ORIGIN; a browser refresh does not load files. If a command fails after saving files, inspect data.saved and data.path, fix the reported issue and reload instead of installing a duplicate or deleting data. Do not toggle unrelated plugins to reload. A new environment variable must be supplied to the running hostdeck process; changing the CLI environment alone does not change the server environment. Restart only when necessary and authorized. For a pure page or link, verify loaded: true in plugin list and check the page URL; when the plugin declares a monitoring card or detail view, use GET /api/cards or GET /api/detail/<id> to verify actual readings. Report files, commands, exit codes and actual verification; distinguish saved files, a loaded plugin and a healthy service.

disk.scanning: Scanning {path}. Browsing shows the last saved reading; results update automatically.
disk.tracking: Hourly tracking is on while hostdeck runs. You can also scan now.
disk.paused: Hourly tracking is paused. Saved history is retained.
disk.unreadable: {count} unreadable entries were not counted. Sizes include only what could be read.
disk.truncated: Directory records reached their limit. The root total is complete for readable files; some subdirectories are not listed.
disk.old: Hourly tracking is on, but the latest reading is more than two hours old.
disk.failure: The last scan failed: {detail}. Saved readings are retained.
disk.barHelp: Red means growth, blue means shrinkage. Select a bar to see which folders changed during that period. Each bar compares its actual recorded endpoints; gaps are not filled.
disk.single: One reading cannot show a change. Scan again, wait for hourly tracking, or choose a longer range.
disk.unknown: The unreadable entries or missing directory summaries differ between readings. The change is unknown; a gap in the curve is not a deletion.
disk.selectedPeriod: Showing direct subfolders for the selected bar’s actual time period.
disk.directoryHelp: Largest changes first. Open a folder to follow its history and direct subfolders.
disk.depthLimit: This is the three-level recording boundary. Deeper files count toward this folder’s size, but are not recorded separately.
disk.noChildren: There are no separately recorded subfolders here. Files directly in this folder still count toward its size.
disk.measurement: Sizes measure disk space occupied by regular files, using decimal units. Links, other volumes and the plugin’s own files are skipped. At most three directory levels and 256 summaries are saved per reading. Times use this browser’s local time zone. The curve uses actual sampling times.
disk.emptyHelp: Confirm Scan now to take the first reading, or start hourly tracking. Opening this page does not scan.
disk.barsKeyboard: Changes by period. Use Left and Right to read, Enter to select, and Escape to clear the selection.
disk.lineKeyboard: Size over time. Use Left and Right to read each scan; all values are also in Scan readings.
disk.scanStarted: Scan started. Results update automatically when the scan finishes.
help.agent.tasks: For scheduled local scripts, use the built-in scheduled-tasks plugin, not a card program or OS task installer. The following commands install a new copy and back up its task configuration; skip installation if plugin list already shows it. Edit the disabled example locally before enabling requested tasks, then reload this exact console. Do not change unrelated tasks. Scripts/interpreters must already exist. The page can save a UTF-8 text file in this plugin's scripts/ folder (one file name, at most 1 MiB). That save does not schedule or run the file. A script row can run that file once without writing tasks.json when a default interpreter exists (python3, node, bash, or powershell -NoProfile -File; Windows uses py -3 for Python and does not run .sh). Schedule opens the task form with the default command filled in. The same page can create, edit and delete tasks in tasks.json; that write refreshes scheduling in this running console and does not start a script. Prefer the file and plugin reload when changing exec.env, exec.dir or the other platform's command: the form keeps those and does not edit them. The example below documents every v1 configuration field. Keep the backup until configuration and actual results are verified, then remove only that backup. Do not edit data/state.json or delete logs to repair errors. Missing environment references must be supplied to the server, not merely this shell. Configuration is strict UTF-8 JSON, at most 1 MiB and 64 tasks, with no unknown/duplicate/null fields. Use five numeric cron fields with an explicit UTC/IANA zone, or every from 1m to 8760h. Timeout defaults to 30m (1s–24h); exec.dir defaults to the plugin folder and exec.windows replaces argv on Windows; exec.env allows only ${env:NAME}. Maximum four simultaneous tasks, one run per task, no queue, catch-up or automatic retry. Pause blocks future starts, Stop selects one run. Use GET /api/detail/scheduled-tasks to verify errors, next time, results and logs; plugin validate validates the manifest, so successful plugin reload is the task configuration check.

observation.source.events: Service management events; these are not application logs.
observation.source.external: No reliable log source was identified. Output may remain in the original terminal.
observation.source.identity_changed: The process identity changed. Following this PID was refused.
observation.source.gone: The entry is no longer listed; its current state is unknown.
observation.source.terminal: Output remains in the original terminal. Hostdeck does not read terminal output.
observation.source.captured: Output collected by Hostdeck for this run.
observation.source.capture_failed: Log capture failed or could not be confirmed; service health is unknown.
observation.result.unknown: The operation result is unknown. Check its state before trying again.
observation.source.configuration_unreada: Could not read the task configuration, so log paths cannot be confirmed.
observation.source.configuration_missing: The loaded task provides no configuration path or output file.
observation.source.events_empty: No matching recent service management events. These are not application logs.
observation.source.events_unreadable: Could not read service management events. These are not application logs.
